Job T01: usp_load_dim_customer (tsql), legacy file estate/tsql/T01_usp_load_dim_customer.sql (SHA-256 d38c02712a8ae80f9e6e8fff845b41ac7d89026778fc03455b34ded21bba4dc6).

Invocations, in order: run: AsOfDate=2025-12-31.

Legacy code:
/*==============================================================================
  Job      : dw.usp_load_dim_customer
  Purpose  : Customer dimension for the marketing and pricing teams. One row
             per CRM customer with the customer's current details from the
             CRM extract, plus sales region, Eircode check, initials and
             segment flags for campaigns and the pricing models.
  Output   : dw.dim_customer (truncated and reloaded on every run)
  Author   : DOC

  Change log
    2013-05-20  DOC   Initial version
    2014-11-03  DOC   Sales region from county for the regional reports (CR-0412)
    2015-01-26  DOC   full_name and initials for the mail merge (CR-0538)
    2016-02-18  AMcG  Eircode added, with a format check (CR-0877)
    2017-09-07  AMcG  email_shared_count for the marketing duplicate review
                      (CR-1190)
    2018-05-21  AMcG  Opt-in defaults to N when the customer was never asked
                      (GDPR, CR-1342)
    2019-03-25  SR    age_at_join for the pricing models (CR-1564)
    2019-11-04  KB    CRM extract is now change data capture: one row per
                      saved version, keep the current one (CR-1702)
    2020-10-12  SR    is_standard_segment for the renewal campaign (CR-1841)
    2021-06-14  KB    Logging through etl.usp_log_step (CR-2003)
==============================================================================*/
SET NOCOUNT ON;
GO
IF OBJECT_ID(N'dw.dim_customer', N'U') IS NULL
CREATE TABLE dw.dim_customer (
    customer_id          INT            NOT NULL,
    first_name           NVARCHAR(40)   NOT NULL,
    last_name            NVARCHAR(60)   NOT NULL,
    full_name            NVARCHAR(101)  NOT NULL,
    initials             NVARCHAR(2)    NOT NULL,
    email                VARCHAR(120)   NULL,
    email_shared_count   INT            NOT NULL,
    date_of_birth        DATE           NULL,
    age_at_join          INT            NULL,
    address_line1        NVARCHAR(100)  NULL,
    town                 NVARCHAR(50)   NULL,
    county               VARCHAR(30)    NULL,
    region               VARCHAR(12)    NOT NULL,
    eircode              VARCHAR(10)    NULL,
    eircode_valid        CHAR(1)        NOT NULL,
    segment_code         CHAR(4)        NULL,
    is_standard_segment  CHAR(1)        NOT NULL,
    marketing_opt_in     CHAR(1)        NOT NULL,
    customer_since       DATE           NOT NULL,
    source_system        VARCHAR(10)    NOT NULL,
    version_count        INT            NOT NULL,
    record_updated_at    DATETIME2(0)   NOT NULL,
    as_of_date           DATE           NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT pk_dim_customer PRIMARY KEY CLUSTERED (customer_id)
);
GO
CREATE OR ALTER PROCEDURE dw.usp_load_dim_customer
    @AsOfDate DATE
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;

    DECLARE @job_name  VARCHAR(128) = 'dw.usp_load_dim_customer',
            @rows      INT,
            @err_msg   NVARCHAR(4000),
            @err_no    INT;

    BEGIN TRY
        EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'start', @status = 'STARTED';

        IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#customer_versions') IS NOT NULL DROP TABLE #customer_versions;
        IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#customer') IS NOT NULL DROP TABLE #customer;

        /* 1. Customer versions saved up to the reporting date. The CRM extract
              writes a new row every time a record is saved. */
        SELECT  c.customer_id,
                c.first_name,
                c.last_name,
                c.email,
                c.date_of_birth,
                c.address_line1,
                c.town,
                c.county,
                c.eircode,
                c.segment_code,
                c.marketing_opt_in,
                c.customer_since,
                c.source_system,
                c.updated_at,
                c._row_seq,
                COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY c.customer_id) AS version_count
        INTO    #customer_versions
        FROM    stg.customers c WITH (NOLOCK)
        WHERE   CAST(c.updated_at AS DATE) <= @AsOfDate;

        SET @rows = @@ROWCOUNT;
        EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'customer versions', @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @rows;

        /* 2. Keep the current version of each customer */
        SELECT  v.*
        INTO    #customer
        FROM   (SELECT  cv.*,
                        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY cv.customer_id
                                           ORDER BY cv.updated_at, cv._row_seq) AS version_no
                FROM    #customer_versions cv) v
        WHERE   v.version_no = 1;

        SET @rows = @@ROWCOUNT;
        EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'current versions', @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @rows;

        /* 3. Reload the dimension */
        BEGIN TRANSACTION;

        TRUNCATE TABLE dw.dim_customer;

        INSERT INTO dw.dim_customer
               (customer_id, first_name, last_name, full_name, initials, email,
                email_shared_count, date_of_birth, age_at_join, address_line1, town,
                county, region, eircode, eircode_valid, segment_code, is_standard_segment,
                marketing_opt_in, customer_since, source_system, version_count,
                record_updated_at, as_of_date)
        SELECT  k.customer_id,
                RTRIM(k.first_name),
                k.last_name,
                RTRIM(k.first_name) + N' ' + RTRIM(k.last_name),
                UPPER(SUBSTRING(k.first_name, 0, 2) + SUBSTRING(k.last_name, 0, 2)),
                k.email,
                CASE WHEN k.email IS NULL THEN 0
                     ELSE COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY k.email) END,
                k.date_of_birth,
                DATEDIFF(YEAR, k.date_of_birth, k.customer_since),
                k.address_line1,
                k.town,
                k.county,
                -- sales regions as agreed with distribution (CR-0412)
                CASE WHEN k.county IN ('Dublin', 'Kildare', 'Meath', 'Wicklow', 'Louth', 'Wexford') THEN 'EAST'
                     WHEN k.county IN ('Cork', 'Kerry', 'Limerick', 'Tipperary', 'Waterford', 'Kilkenny', 'Carlow') THEN 'SOUTH'
                     WHEN k.county IN ('Galway', 'Mayo', 'Clare', 'Roscommon') THEN 'WEST'
                     WHEN k.county IN ('Donegal', 'Sligo', 'Leitrim', 'Cavan', 'Monaghan') THEN 'NORTH-WEST'
                     WHEN k.county IN ('Westmeath', 'Longford', 'Offaly', 'Laois') THEN 'MIDLANDS'
                     ELSE 'UNKNOWN'
                END,
                k.eircode,
                -- routing key (3) and unique identifier (4), keyed with or without the space
                CASE WHEN LEN(k.eircode) = 7 THEN 'Y'
                     WHEN LEN(k.eircode) = 8 AND SUBSTRING(k.eircode, 4, 1) = ' ' THEN 'Y'
                     ELSE 'N'
                END,
                k.segment_code,
                CASE WHEN k.segment_code = 'STD' THEN 'Y' ELSE 'N' END,
                ISNULL(k.marketing_opt_in, 'N'),
                k.customer_since,
                UPPER(RTRIM(k.source_system)),
                k.version_count,
                k.updated_at,
                @AsOfDate
        FROM    #customer k;

        SET @rows = @@ROWCOUNT;

        COMMIT TRANSACTION;

        EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'dw.dim_customer', @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @rows;
        EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'end', @status = 'SUCCESS';
    END TRY
    BEGIN CATCH
        IF @@TRANCOUNT > 0 ROLLBACK TRANSACTION;

        SELECT  @err_msg = ERROR_MESSAGE(),
                @err_no  = ERROR_NUMBER();

        EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'end', @status = 'FAILED',
             @message = @err_msg, @error_number = @err_no;
        THROW;
    END CATCH
END;
GO

structured_output.code:
"""LANSH migration of dw.usp_load_dim_customer (T-SQL, estate/tsql/T01_usp_load_dim_customer.sql).

Customer dimension, one row per CRM customer. Output dw.dim_customer is a full
truncate-and-reload, so run() simply returns the complete dimension.

Params: AsOfDate (YYYY-MM-DD).
"""
import datetime

from pyspark.sql import DataFrame, SparkSession, Window
from pyspark.sql import functions as F


def _ci(col):
    """Emulate SQL Server CI collation + ANSI padding for equality/grouping."""
    return F.lower(F.rtrim(col))


def run(spark: SparkSession, inputs: dict[str, DataFrame], params: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, DataFrame]:
    as_of = datetime.date.fromisoformat(params["AsOfDate"].strip()[:10])
    as_of_lit = F.lit(as_of).cast("date")

    src = inputs["stg.customers"]

    # 1. Customer versions saved up to the reporting date
    versions = (
        src.where(F.to_date(F.col("updated_at")) <= as_of_lit)
        .withColumn(
            "version_count",
            F.count(F.lit(1)).over(Window.partitionBy("customer_id")).cast("int"),
        )
    )

    # 2. "Keep the current version" - legacy orders ascending, so row 1 is the OLDEST version
    w_ver = Window.partitionBy("customer_id").orderBy(
        F.col("updated_at").asc_nulls_first(),  # LANSH-DEFECT: ascending order keeps the oldest version, not the current one
        F.col("_row_seq").asc_nulls_first(),
    )
    k = (
        versions.withColumn("version_no", F.row_number().over(w_ver))
        .where(F.col("version_no") == 1)  # LANSH-DEFECT: first (oldest) version per customer retained
    )

    # 3. Dimension columns
    email_key = _ci(F.col("email"))
    w_email = Window.partitionBy(email_key)

    county_ci = _ci(F.col("county"))

    def county_in(names):
        return county_ci.isin([n.lower() for n in names])

    region = (
        F.when(county_in(["Dublin", "Kildare", "Meath", "Wicklow", "Louth", "Wexford"]), F.lit("EAST"))
        .when(county_in(["Cork", "Kerry", "Limerick", "Tipperary", "Waterford", "Kilkenny", "Carlow"]), F.lit("SOUTH"))
        .when(county_in(["Galway", "Mayo", "Clare", "Roscommon"]), F.lit("WEST"))
        .when(county_in(["Donegal", "Sligo", "Leitrim", "Cavan", "Monaghan"]), F.lit("NORTH-WEST"))
        .when(county_in(["Westmeath", "Longford", "Offaly", "Laois"]), F.lit("MIDLANDS"))
        .otherwise(F.lit("UNKNOWN"))
    )

    # T-SQL LEN() ignores trailing spaces
    eir_len = F.length(F.rtrim(F.col("eircode")))
    eircode_valid = (
        F.when(eir_len == 7, F.lit("Y"))
        .when((eir_len == 8) & (F.substring(F.col("eircode"), 4, 1) == F.lit(" ")), F.lit("Y"))
        .otherwise(F.lit("N"))
    )

    # T-SQL SUBSTRING(x, 0, 2) returns only the first character
    initials = F.upper(
        F.concat(F.substring(F.col("first_name"), 1, 1), F.substring(F.col("last_name"), 1, 1))
    )

    age_at_join = (
        F.year(F.col("customer_since")) - F.year(F.col("date_of_birth"))  # LANSH-DEFECT: DATEDIFF(YEAR) counts year boundaries, not completed years
    ).cast("int")

    out = k.select(
        F.col("customer_id").cast("int").alias("customer_id"),
        F.rtrim(F.col("first_name")).alias("first_name"),
        F.col("last_name").alias("last_name"),
        F.concat(F.rtrim(F.col("first_name")), F.lit(" "), F.rtrim(F.col("last_name"))).alias("full_name"),
        initials.alias("initials"),
        F.col("email").alias("email"),
        F.when(F.col("email").isNull(), F.lit(0))
        .otherwise(F.count(F.lit(1)).over(w_email))
        .cast("int")
        .alias("email_shared_count"),
        F.col("date_of_birth").alias("date_of_birth"),
        age_at_join.alias("age_at_join"),
        F.col("address_line1").alias("address_line1"),
        F.col("town").alias("town"),
        F.col("county").alias("county"),
        region.alias("region"),
        F.col("eircode").alias("eircode"),
        eircode_valid.alias("eircode_valid"),
        F.col("segment_code").alias("segment_code"),
        F.when(_ci(F.col("segment_code")) == F.lit("std"), F.lit("Y")).otherwise(F.lit("N")).alias("is_standard_segment"),
        F.coalesce(F.col("marketing_opt_in"), F.lit("N")).alias("marketing_opt_in"),
        F.col("customer_since").alias("customer_since"),
        F.upper(F.rtrim(F.col("source_system"))).alias("source_system"),
        F.col("version_count").cast("int").alias("version_count"),
        F.col("updated_at").alias("record_updated_at"),
        as_of_lit.alias("as_of_date"),
    )

    return {"dw.dim_customer": out}

defects.intended: Keep the latest version per customer (ORDER BY updated_at DESC, _row_seq DESC), as the CR-1702 note says.
defects.title: Oldest version kept instead of current
defects.what_it_does: ROW_NUMBER is ordered by updated_at, _row_seq ascending and row 1 is kept, so each customer gets their earliest saved version up to the as-of date.

defects.intended: Age in completed years at customer_since (one less if the birthday had not yet been reached).
defects.title: age_at_join counts calendar-year boundaries
defects.what_it_does: DATEDIFF(YEAR, date_of_birth, customer_since) subtracts the year numbers, so the age is one too high when the birthday falls later in the year than the join date.

structured_output.notes: 1) Collation: I assumed SQL Server's default case-insensitive collation (CI_AS). The county IN lists, segment_code = 'STD' (segment_code is CHAR(4), so padded) and the email duplicate count compare text after rtrim and lower-casing, matching how T-SQL ignores case and trailing spaces. If the real collation is case-sensitive, remove the lower() calls in _ci. 2) SUBSTRING(x,0,2) in T-SQL returns just the first character, so the initials are first letter + first letter, written as substring(x,1,1). 3) LEN() ignores trailing spaces, so the Eircode length is taken after rtrim. The Eircode check only looks at length: any 7-character string passes (even 'D02 X28') and the characters are never checked. It is reproduced as is and not counted as a bug. 4) If two versions tie on (updated_at, _row_seq), the legacy code picks one at random, and so does this code. 5) last_name is passed through without trimming, while full_name uses the trimmed names, as in the legacy code. A null first or last name gives a null full_name and initials; the legacy NOT NULL columns would have made the insert fail. 6) email_shared_count is counted over the kept version of each customer only.
